chapter.title: Quantity: Counting and Measuring (Alt: Quantities and Change

section.title: The Integers \mathbb{Z}
section.p: The integers are the basic number system we are all familiar with, positive and negative whole numbers, and zero. We can solve any additive equation in this system.

statement.p: For any integers a and b, we can always solve the equation x + a = b for the unknown integer x

example.p: The solution to x+1=5 is x=4
The solution to x+4=7 is x=3
The solution to x+12=7 is x=-5

section.p: Notice we need negative numbers to be able to solve any addition equation. If we only had positive numbers, then we can only solve equations when a \le b.

example.p: What about solving the equation 3\cdot x + 2 = 16, for an unknown integer x?
This equation cannot be solved: we can subtract 2 from both sides to get 3\cdot x = 14, but there is no integer x that solves this equation since 3 does not divide 14

section.title: The Rationals \mathbb{Q}
section.p: Now we can solve linear equations... (almost, multiplication by 0...)

statement.p: Write a computer program that will implement the Euclidean algorithm. The program should accept two positive integers a and b as input and should output \gcd( a,b) as well as integers r and s such that \gcd( a,b) = ra + sb.
